qs.q: A patient with von Willebrand disease needs factor replacement but concentrates are unavailable. Which product is the best alternative?
o: Fresh frozen plasma administered intravenously
Packed red blood cells administered intravenously
Platelet concentrate administered intravenously
Whole blood administered intravenously
Cryoprecipitate administered intravenously
qs.e: Cryoprecipitate contains high levels of Factor VIII and vWF.
qs.s: Weekly Year 3: Blood Transfusion Exam - November 6, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A 26-year-old woman with known von Willebrand disease reports worsening menorrhagia since menarche and a normal pelvic exam. Which investigation is most appropriate to evaluate her bleeding severity?
o: Serum iron level and ferritin measurement
Comprehensive coagulation test panel
Transvaginal ultrasound imaging of uterus
Endometrial tissue biopsy procedure
qs.e: Targeted coagulation studies are essential to assess the severity of her known underlying bleeding disorder. Imaging and tissue biopsy are not indicated for an inherited coagulopathy with normal pelvic anatomy.

qs.q: A patient with severe von Willebrand disease requires emergency surgery, but specific factor concentrates are unavailable in the facility. Which alternative blood product contains adequate high-molecular-weight multimers to correct hemostasis?
o: Fresh frozen plasma rich in stable coagulation factors
Liquid plasma possessing depleted labile factor components
Cryoprecipitate containing concentrated fibrinogen and VIII
Washed red blood cells lacking residual plasma proteins
Platelet rich plasma harvested from healthy donors
qs.e: Cryoprecipitate precipitates out high concentrations of factor VIII, von Willebrand factor, and fibrinogen during thawing.
qs.s: Weekly Year 3: Blood Transfusion Exam - October 30, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: What blood component is prepared by thawing fresh frozen plasma (FFP) at 4 degrees Celsius and is specifically indicated for fibrinogen deficiency, von Willebrand disease, or factor VIII deficiency?
o: Cryoprecipitate
Packed red cells
Granulocyte concentrate
Whole blood unit
qs.e: Cryoprecipitate is collected when FFP is thawed at 4 degrees, refrozen, and stored up to 1 year; it is used in fibrinogen deficiency, von Willebrand disease, and factor VIII, XIII, or DIC states.

qs.q: A patient with von Willebrand disease requires factor VIII replacement. Which product is suitable for this purpose, especially in small volumes for children?
o: Platelet concentrate units
Human albumin solution
Packed red blood cells
Freeze-dried factor VIII
qs.e: Freeze-dried Factor VIII concentrates are used for hemophilia A and von Willebrand disease and are ideal for children due to their small volume. Packed red cells and platelets do not provide factor VIII replacement.
qs.s: Transfusion: Governance, Donor Selection & Blood Groups: MCQs

qs.q: A patient with severe von Willebrand disease is undergoing emergency surgery and requires factor replacement therapy, but specific factor concentrates are unavailable. Which blood product is the most appropriate alternative?
o: Fresh frozen plasma for acute volume expansion
Cryoprecipitate for fibrinogen and factor replacement
Platelet concentrates for active thrombocytopenia
Prothrombin complex concentrate for warfarin reversal
qs.e: Cryoprecipitate contains high concentrations of fibrinogen, Factor VIII, Factor XIII, and von Willebrand factor, making it useful for Haemophilia A and hypofibrinogenaemia. It does not contain platelets or albumin.

qs.q: A patient with von Willebrand disease typically presents with which pattern of laboratory results?
o: Normal bleeding time but an increased prothrombin time
Lengthened bleeding time together with a prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time
Reduced platelet count while the activated partial thromboplastin time remains normal
Extended prothrombin time with a normal activated partial thromboplastin time
qs.e: vWD causes prolonged bleeding time due to impaired platelet adhesion and prolonged aPTT because vWF carries and protects Factor VIII. PT is normal as the extrinsic pathway is unaffected.

qs.q: A 22-year-old woman with a mild bleeding diathesis undergoes treatment with desmopressin (DDAVP) prior to dental extraction. How does this pharmacologic agent control bleeding in mild von Willebrand disease?
o: Directly substitutes for the missing factor VIII
Suppresses excessive platelet aggregation activity
Triggers release of stored von Willebrand factor
Stimulates megakaryopoiesis in the bone marrow
qs.e: DDAVP stimulates the release of stored von Willebrand factor and Factor VIII from endothelial cells, raising their levels. It does not directly replace factors or inhibit platelets.
